className.description: Space-separated CSS classes for the line, e.g. "plain" for normal text instead of the bar's inverse video

anyOf.description: A bar line with text or links at its left, middle and right

waitForReveal.description: Make links, toggles, sliders, sections and prompts usable only once the whole screen has revealed, as on a real terminal, rather than each as it appears. At a pause, those revealed so far work while it waits. A tap still finishes the reveal at once (default: false)

glitch.description: Default glitch options, for reveals and transitions

duration.description: Milliseconds a glitch takes (default: 1000)

defaults.description: Default options for each kind of reveal

additionalProperties.description: true or false, a number, or text

variables.description: The program's variables and their starting values: true or false, a number, or text. Actions change them with `set`, toggles, sliders and prompts can be bound to them, `if` tests them, and text shows them as "{name}". They reset when the page reloads.

to.description: Seconds it stops at: lower than from to count down, higher to count up (default: 0)

format.description: How the time is shown: "mm:ss", "hh:mm:ss" or "ss" (default: "mm:ss")

onComplete.description: What happens when it reaches to

autostart.description: Start running when the program does, rather than at a "startTimer" action (default: false)

additionalProperties.description: A clock that keeps running from screen to screen: started, stopped and reset by actions ("startTimer", "stopTimer", "resetTimer"), shown in text as "{name}" and by timer elements, and tested by conditions as its seconds. Its onComplete runs on whatever screen the player is on.

timers.description: The program's timers, by name: clocks that keep running from screen to screen, such as a self-destruct countdown

skipKeys.description: Keys that finish revealing the screen at once, like a click, when the program doesn't use them for anything else: key names like "Escape" or "Space", or [] for none. In kiosk mode, Esc also leaves full screen, so try ["Space"] (default: ["Escape"])

alert.description: Color of text with the "alert" class (default: "#ff3c00")

shadow.description: The shadow text casts: a CRT's "glow", a dark "drop" shadow, an LCD's segments' faint "lcd" shadow, ink's slight "ink" bleed, or "none" (default: "glow")

stripes.description: Bands of this color behind every other three lines, scrolling with the text, like green-bar printer paper (default: none)

sprockets.description: Sprocket holes down both sides, scrolling with the text, like fanfold printer paper; left out on narrow screens (default: false)

capitals.description: Show every letter as a capital, as an LCD would, however it's written (default: false)

anyOf.description: Your own colors

theme.description: The color scheme: "default" (pale blue on black), "amber", "green" or "white"; a look of its own, with a font and effects: "vcr" (a VCR's blue menu), "lcd" (an LCD's segments), "paper" (typed) or "printout" (dot matrix, on green-bar paper); "contrast-dark" or "contrast-light", for legibility; or your own colors (default: "default")

font.description: The typeface: a period PC font; a VCR's ("home-video"), an LCD's segments ("digit-tech"), a dot-matrix printer's ("matrixtype") or a typewriter's ("x-typewriter"); or one installed on the player's computer ("courier-new", "consolas" on Windows, "menlo" on macOS; the browser's own monospace font where it isn't) (default: the theme's, or "departure-mono")

fontScale.description: How big text is, from 0.5 (half the usual size) to 2 (twice). A pixel font still snaps to whole multiples of its pixels, so it grows in steps (default: 0.75)

lineSpacing.description: How far apart lines are, as a multiple of the text's size, from 1 (touching, so block art and box drawing join up, as on the original machines) to 2 (default: 1.25)

characters.description: Characters shown as others, e.g. { "<": "(", "█": "#" }: for a font without some character, or just for the look. Only what's shown changes, one character for one, so text keeps its shape; commands, conditions and what players type are matched as written.

src.description: An image, relative to the page, e.g. "data/pointers/claw.png": a PNG, about 32×32 pixels at most (bigger ones may be ignored)

x.description: The column of the pixel that points, from the left (default: 0)

y.description: The row of the pixel that points, from the top (default: 0)

anyOf.description: A pointer of your own: an image, and the pixel in it that points

pointer.description: The mouse pointer: "system" (the browser's own), "theme" (a pixel arrow in the theme's colors), "block" (a character cell that jumps from cell to cell, as in DOS), "crosshair" (lines across the whole screen), "hidden", or an image of your own. Not on touch screens; players can switch back to their own in quick settings (default: "system")

opacity.description: Strength of the lines, from 0 to 1 (default: 0.5)

moving.description: Roll a bright line down the screen (default: true)

anyOf.description: CRT scanlines, with an optional rolling band. On by default.

scale.description: Size of a noise pixel, in screen pixels (default: 3)

radius.description: How far the glow spreads, in pixels (default: 8)

offset.description: How far the colors split, in pixels (default: 1)

anyOf.description: Red and cyan fringes on text, like misaligned color guns. Off by default.

typing.description: Key clicks as text types in (default: true)

key.description: Key click: Each character typed, and keys pressed in a prompt

glitch.description: Glitch: Glitch reveals and the glitch transition

hiss.description: Static hiss: Under the static effect, as loud as the static is strong

select.description: Select: Links, toggles, dialog buttons, known commands

tick.description: Slider tick: A slider moving a step

alert.description: Alert: A dialog with the "alert" class opening

error.description: Error: A command the prompt doesn't know

voices.description: Adjustments to Teletronix's own sounds, overriding their defaults. Tune them by ear on the editor (?edit, Sounds, Built-in tab) and paste the result here.

anyOf.description: Sound options: the volume, and each kind of sound on or off

sound.description: Generated retro sound effects: true, false, or an object of options. On by default; players can mute them with the sound toggle.
